physicalNotes: Radius 0.17842805 Jupiter radii from Hirano et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..127H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract): 12,756.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0147 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): P 10.59366 d
sources.shape: Hirano et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..127H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HIRANO_ET_AL__2018): a/R* 32.2; Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): inclination derived from its transit duration 2.4 h and Rp/R* 0.0437 with its a/R* 31.2 (Winn 2010, eqs. 14 and 16)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): transit mid-time 2457402.5547 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 342 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
